US_10Y_YIELD.name: US 10-Year Treasury Yield
US_10Y_YIELD.description: The benchmark risk-free rate. Rising yields increase the discount rate used to value future earnings, compressing P/E multiples on high-growth stocks. Also makes dividend-paying stocks (utilities, REITs) relatively less attractive.

FED_FUNDS_RATE_PROXY.name: US 13-Week Treasury Bill (Fed Funds Proxy)
FED_FUNDS_RATE_PROXY.description: Short end of the yield curve; closely tracks the Federal Reserve's policy rate. Banks profit when the spread between short-term borrowing costs and long-term lending rates (net interest margin) is wide.

YIELD_CURVE_10Y2Y.name: US 10Y-2Y Yield Spread (Yield Curve)
YIELD_CURVE_10Y2Y.description: The spread between 10-year and 2-year Treasury yields. When inverted (negative), it historically predicts recession within 12-18 months. Steep curve benefits banks (borrow short, lend long). Flat/inverted curve squeezes bank margins.

VIX.name: CBOE Volatility Index (VIX)
VIX.description: Market's 30-day expected volatility derived from S&P 500 options. Often called the 'fear gauge.' VIX above 30 signals high fear; below 15 signals complacency. Spikes in VIX trigger risk-off flows into bonds and defensive sectors.

WTI_CRUDE_OIL.name: WTI Crude Oil (front-month futures)
WTI_CRUDE_OIL.description: West Texas Intermediate crude oil price. Direct input cost for airlines, chemicals, and plastics. Higher oil prices expand margins for E&P companies and oilfield services but squeeze consumer discretionary spending power.

USD_INDEX.name: US Dollar Index (DXY)
USD_INDEX.description: Measures the USD against a basket of major currencies. A strong dollar makes US exports more expensive abroad, reducing the dollar-value of international revenue for US multinationals (tech, pharma, industrials). Typically inverse to commodities priced in USD.

GOLD.name: Gold (front-month futures)
GOLD.description: Flight-to-safety asset. Rises during geopolitical stress, inflation fears, or dollar weakness. Directly impacts gold miners (NEM). Generally moves inverse to real interest rates.

COPPER.name: Copper (front-month futures)
COPPER.description: 'Dr. Copper' — historically one of the best leading indicators of global economic health due to its use in construction, EVs, and electronics. Falling copper prices often signal slowing global demand.

NATURAL_GAS.name: Natural Gas (front-month futures)
NATURAL_GAS.description: Key fuel for power generation and industrial processes. High natural gas prices help E&P and midstream companies but hurt utilities and energy-intensive manufacturers.

SP500.name: S&P 500 Index
SP500.description: Broad US equity market benchmark. All S&P 500 stocks show strong positive beta to this index.
